topicName: Rootless Mode and User Namespace Isolation
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Rootless Mode and User Namespace Isolation in Docker"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Running Docker in rootless mode allows you to run the Docker daemon and containers as a non-root user to mitigate potential container breakout vulnerabilities. This tutorial covers the prerequisites, installation steps, and verification of rootless Docker using Linux user namespaces."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and System Requirements"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before setting up rootless Docker, ensure your Linux distribution meets the necessary requirements. You need a standard user account with sudo privileges for initial setup, and your kernel must support user namespaces."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Linux distribution with kernel version 4.18 or later (5.0+ recommended)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Package dependencies: uidmap, dbus-user-session, and iptables."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Installing Prerequisites"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Log into your non-root user account and install the required packages. The uidmap package is critical because it provides shadow-utils tools (newuidmap and newgidmap) necessary for user namespace mapping."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y uidmap dbus-user-session iptables"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring Sub-UID and Sub-GID Ranges"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"User namespaces require the allocating user to have a range of assigned UIDs and GIDs in /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid. Verify that your user has entries configured."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"grep \"^$(whoami):\" /etc/subuid || echo \"$(whoami):100000:65536\" | sudo tee -a /etc/subuid"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Installing Rootless Docker"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Run the official rootless installation script provided by Docker. This script sets up systemd user services and the necessary binaries inside your home directory."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Configuring Environment Variables"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To interact with the rootless Docker daemon, you must export the DOCKER_HOST environment variable. Add this configuration to your shell profile (~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc)."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"export DOCKER_HOST=\"unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock\""},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Verifying the Setup"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Run the docker info command to verify that the daemon is successfully running in rootless mode."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"docker info"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Look for \"SecurityOptions: rootless\" in the output. If this is present, your Docker daemon is isolated using user namespaces and operates securely without root privileges."}]
